central_question: What will the LME copper cash settlement price (USD per tonne) be on 31 December 2027, expressed as a probability-weighted central forecast with P10/P50/P90 levels (forecaster central: P50 ≈ $13,400/t, weighted mean $13,750/t, P10 ≈ $9,900/t, P90 ≈ $18,300/t)?

situation_brief.current_situation: Copper is in a record regime: LME cash around $14,415–14,751/t in October 2026, the IMF monthly series at 14,473.0559 USD/t for 2026-09 (+44.8% y/y). A concentrate-led squeeze dominates: the 2026 Antofagasta–Jiangxi TC benchmark settled at $0/t and the SMM imported concentrate index is deeply negative (−$231.68/dmt on 30 Sep 2026). COMEX warehouses hold >714,000 t (~70% of visible stocks) stranded behind 50% Section 232 tariffs, while LME stocks are 229,650–273,750 t; combined exchange cover ≈ 0.4 months of world consumption. ICSG (14 Oct 2026) forecasts a 104,000 t refined surplus in 2026 widening to 368,000 t in 2027.
situation_brief.context: Chinese smelting overcapacity presses against scarce mine supply. ICSG projects mine growth of 1.3% in 2026 and 3.1% in 2027 on a Cobre Panama restart plus Kamoa-Kakula, QB2 and Chilean ramps. Chinese refined output grew 4% y/y Jan–Aug 2026 despite the CSPT's November 2025 pledge to cut >10%, cushioned by sulphuric-acid and gold/silver byproducts. The LME December 2027 prompt anchors the market mid at $14,650/t (14 Oct 2026); Goldman's 2027 average is $15,400/t after a $3,700/t upward revision in nine months.
situation_brief.dynamics: Record prices coexist with a realized ICSG surplus (+218 kt Jan–Aug 2026) because metal is stranded in US warehouses and ex-US refined supply is capped by negative TCs, Q4 2026 smelter maintenance (~80,000 t cut), a scrap-tax crackdown and concentrate import declines (−4.1% y/y in Sep 2026). The 2027 balance hinges on whether mine increments and smelter discipline rebuild TCs toward zero or the squeeze persists into end-2027.
fault_lines: Concentrate shortage vs mine-supply ramp (Squeeze persists 40% vs Supply catches up 30%)
US Section 232 tariff dislocation and the Annex III sunset landing exactly on 31 Dec 2027
Chinese smelter overcapacity vs CSPT output-cut compliance under negative TCs
State stockpiling (SRB, US Project Vault ~$12bn) vs countercyclical 2021 release precedent
Decelerating demand (China below 2%) vs electrification build-outs (grid, EV, datacentres)
Cobre Panama restart: commission recommended negotiations 30 Sep 2026, no scope or timing set
catalysts: 2027 Antofagasta–Chinese smelter TC/RC benchmark at Asia Copper Week, 17–19 Nov 2026
Q4 2026 Chinese smelter maintenance (~80,000 t) and scrap-tax crackdown
Cobre Panama restart negotiations with First Quantum
Rolling Section 232 additions by US Commerce/USTR; Annex III sunset 31 Dec 2027
SMM weekly concentrate index path (recovery above −$100 vs deeper lows)
LME stock builds vs draws; COMEX–LME spread re-widening
Kamoa-Kakula 2027 delivery on 500,000–540,000 t guidance; Cochilco's +5.2% Chile rebound

scenarios.name: Squeeze persists
scenarios.narrative: Concentrate shortage and smelter curtailments keep the refined market in deficit, stocks stay tight and copper holds or extends above the $13,000-16,000 regime by end-2027; prior: copper 20-25% annual volatility around an elevated spot.

scenarios.name: Supply catches up
scenarios.narrative: Cobre Panama restart plus project ramp-ups and Chinese capacity discipline flip the balance to surplus per ICSG 2027, easing prices back toward $11,000-13,000; prior: deficits historically resolve within 18-24 months of high prices.

scenarios.name: Supercycle breakout
scenarios.narrative: Tariff escalation, SRB buying or a major supply shock plus demand acceleration drives copper above $18,000; prior: ~1-sigma tail under 20-25% volatility from a $14,400 base.

scenarios.name: Demand recession
scenarios.narrative: A global or Chinese downturn plus high-price demand destruction pulls copper below $11,000; prior: ~1-sigma downside tail.
